225.text: You are in the basement of the stairwell. "Hmmm...: It's pretty dark down here!" you observe with an expert eye, since you can barely see a thing (man! What a sentence!). Above your head is the middle floor of the castle, from which you descended here. You shiver as you realise that Zargon is probably down here on this floor too - hiding behind one of those walls, maybe just a few yards from you, just waiting for you to rush unsuspectingly into his chamber without suspecting the slightest danger - and you can be damn sure that he won't be alone...! The passage leads north into a corridor, east into an armoury, and south into the gatekeeper's office.

Apparently, King Richard's brave retainers didn't even have time to prepare for their final, cruel battle: they were treacherously attacked from behind and slaughtered like cattle! In the corner stands a life-size statue of a seasoned old warrior in full armour. You can only leave the armoury through the west door, which leads back into the stairwell.

227.text: You enter a gloomy hall. Yes, really, that's about all I can tell you. It's a plain tunnel whose sole purpose is to connect two rooms we had to build round a corner. Know what I mean? Yes? Oh, come off it! Of course you DON'T: you haven't drawn a map, have you? Thought not! Still, I hope you'll forgive this little workaround. You've made it this far without any serious trouble (yes, SERIOUS! If only you knew what's still waiting for you...) and hopefully spent a few enjoyable hours in our little world. Now that this rambling nonsense has once again padded out a room description, here's everything we managed to think of about this place in three years of development: a curtain hangs on the wall to your right, hiding the passage to the castle's wine cellar. Further north, an eerie phosphorescent glow shines in the darkness. Frightening, isn't it? I mean, frightening how so little information can fill so much mindless text!

Whatever fine vintage once filled the three huge wooden barrels against the western wall, the sour stuff in them now wouldn't win so much as a consolation prize in WINZER! One barrel looks oddly familiar, though you can't quite remember where you've seen it before... Slippery stone steps in the northeastern corner lead back to the pantry on the castle's ground floor.

229.text: You enter a corridor in the basement of the castle. Right in front of you rises a huge black ebony door, eerily bathed in the glow of torches mounted on the walls. Oddly enough, the otherwise rough, rocky floor for a metre in front of the door is neatly tiled: this is where the living quarters seem to start again. Now you can either go back to the stone steps in the south or try to open the door in the north - if it isn't already open... As you happen to look up, you see two dirty grey birds circling high overhead in a blue sky: "Vultures!", flashes through your mind... Have you lost it? We are several metres underground! Maybe you should just stop taking those dreadful drugs?

230.text: You enter a long, gloomy hall lined with some mysterious stone boxes. Exactly in the middle of the vault someone has drawn a large pentagram on the floor. After your eyes have gotten used to the darkness down here, your blood runs cold when you look at the large containers again! These "boxes" are somehow too big and massive for ordinary chests or the like! They can only be... COFFINS! You break out in a cold sweat of fear: "NO! Please, not again!" You fervently beg the A.C.A gods - but they show no mercy: Coffins they are, and coffins they're staying! And now you finally notice the penetrating smell of rot and decay in the air - the sweet scent of death, which oozes out of every crack in the stone sarcophagi in thick, light green clouds of smoke... The only visible way out of this room is the portal in the south, which will lead you back to the lobby.

But what really catches your eye is his pitch-black four-poster bed with its red velvet curtains. Perhaps we could hold his teddy bear hostage...? The eastern door leads back to Zargon's Black Library.

The shelves bow under the weight of ancient, yellowed tomes. Here you'll find just about everything any deranged mind has ever put to paper about devil worship, death cults and similar nonsense. Apart from the shelves, the room contains a large antique leather armchair and a matching study table. A candle set in a smashed human skull casts a restless, flickering light across the room... There are exits in all four directions. You may just have to find them first...

The only way out of this unholy place is through the eastern door.

236.text: Carefully, desperately trying not to make a sound, you enter the evil sorcerer Zargon's inner sanctum. Purple, green and turquoise smoke billows from the cauldrons, taking the shapes of demons, spirits and devils. They converse in a language as alien to you as the world whose inhabitants spoke it millions of years ago. Whatever they're saying, it sounds truly diabolical! In the northwestern corner stands a pedestal with a black velvet cushion for Zargon's Soul Crystal: the jewel that grants him his unholy power and holds him captive forever! The only way out of this unnerving chaos of voices and colours is the black ebony door in the western wall.

237.text: You are in the gatekeeper's house. Like all other servants at the king's court, he seems to have been a Butah dwarf, which can be easily seen from the size of his small wooden hut: when you enter it you have to bend low to avoid banging your head on the door frame! The tiny size of the furniture confirms your assumptions: Even the relatively generously sized bed would be too small for you to be able to sit on it even remotely comfortably! Otherwise, however, the entire living space is quite sparsely furnished, albeit not nearly as primitive as the other rooms in this cave system might lead one to expect. Through the small door in the north wall you can get back to the shore of the small island.

You can exit the ferry house through the door in the eastern wall.

But since you don't meet the conditions that would entitle you to drink from the spring anyway, the meaning of the sign doesn't really matter to you... You can continue your way north or west.

Well, buddy: good luck! Exits lead in all directions except north - the only question left is how you're going to reach them...

249.text: It seems the rats don't have quite as much time to waste as you do, because it's supper time and the fat beasts seem to know it perfectly well: as if on cue, they all jump at you at once! You can barely fend off the little beasts' relentless attacks and you are thrown to the ground, where you have to watch helplessly as they turn you into a tasty rat supper! Well: It's really a pretty bad feeling to have an eye ripped out of your head while you're still alive: the pain almost drives you insane! But just as you open your mouth to roar loudly, a rat jumps onto your face, dances there to hot, ritualistic rhythms - and spins into a pirouette, cries an ecstatic "Ouh!" and tears out your tongue with a flourish so that your scream is muffled by a warm gush of your own blood to a gurgling rattle! Don't worry, you won't choke on it! Because with your remaining eye you can already see a third rat sniffing your carotid artery curiously before it finally cuts it through with a single, hearty bite of its razor-sharp incisors and puts you out of your misery...

In the desperate hope of getting an opportunity to escape during the competition, you agree to a match - until it is made absolutely clear to you that you should not take part in the game as an athlete, but as a ROPE! Well, your body wasn't exactly competition-grade equipment, because it tears after only two rounds of determined tugging, so that there are now two halves of you, spilling ruptured intestines, blood and bile over the nice, clean floor...

251.text: When you materialize again in the middle of the white pentagram in Zargon's inner sanctum, the old sorcerer rises from his high-backed chair in amazement. "Why did you have to come so early?", he rasps with a hint of disappointment in his voice, "I don't have any time at the moment to take care of you - unfortunately...!" With a casual flick of his right hand, he creates a huge fireball in the air out of nowhere and hurls it right at you! The last thing you can think about in the remaining time is Zargon's extreme waste of energy - because a modest little lightning bolt would probably have done it! Then it suddenly becomes very bright - and very hot! In the end, a small pile of smoking ash is all that's left of your body...

252.text: When Zargon sees you appear in the middle of his white chalk pentagram, he gets up and rises to his full height: "Why couldn't you wait?" he snarls in disappointment, "I have absolutely no time for you at the moment - unfortunately..." With a slight flick of his right hand, he attempts to summon a fireball, but all you can see is a small flame scorching his palms! As you giggle gleefully, the sorcerer screams in pain, "Damn! But you haven't won yet!" He claps his hands briefly ("Say hooo!"), and a few seconds later two huge, ugly mummies materialize in the pentagram next to you. Completely shocked and unable to defend yourself, you don't cause them the slightest problem: Strong claws grab your throat, and shortly thereafter you hear your neck snap with a short, loud "CRACK!"! "Thank God!" you think with relief, "I was afraid they would strangle me!" As your soul departs for the happy hunting grounds, you watch as your head is brutally ripped from your torso and smashed to the ground, where your brains ooze across the flagstones until Zargon has someone mop them up...

253.text: If you thought Zargon would be frightened when you burst into his secret chambers, you've got another think coming! He calmly finishes his conversation with a demon lord before even turning to you. After sizing you up for a few seconds, he shouts, "Out! Now! Do you think I'd let you wander round my castle for hours just to slaughter you without having a little fun first? You haven't a hope of beating me yet! Get out and prepare properly for our fight! I'm entitled to some enjoyment, you know. A fellow has to treat himself occasionally..." He shoves you angrily through the doorway and shuts the door. Outside, you can still hear him muttering: "Young fools! Not the faintest idea what they're doing, but always charging in headfirst! How does that idiot expect to get onto the high-score table? I really must have a word with Chris and Kai. Putting me in this stupid game was bad enough, but sending me wimps like that is beyond a joke! I ought to complain to the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Non-Player Characters..."

255.text: Noticing the Butah King's cloak around your shoulders, the old ferryman falls to his knees and asks in a submissive voice, "Your Majesty wishes to use the boat?" After he has licked your feet clean, the ferry captain goes back to his work with countless bows. You see: clothes make the man!

269.text: Zargon sees you looking towards his Soul Crystal and tries to reach the pedestal first. Too late! In two or three nimble strides, you're there. You seize the jewel and raise it above your head. It pulses heavily in your hands, as though alive! Realising that you now hold power over him, Zargon starts to beg. He pleads for his life, offers you Mylgor's position as governor of the village, and even promises to make you human again if you'll spare the crystal. Somewhere, he says, there is a spring whose water can cure the infection of werewolf blood... For a moment you think back over everything that has happened. Which matters more: your own fate, or that of the villagers he has tormented and enslaved? The decision doesn't take long. Ignoring his whining, you hurl the Soul Crystal to the floor. It shatters into a thousand splinters, each still reflecting Zargon's face! At that very instant, he screams behind you. You spin round to see him struggling for his life inside a dense, dark grey cloud, released from the shattered jewel where it must have waited for decades for this one moment. Only his wildly flailing arms and legs protrude from the murk! Then, suddenly, it is over. The cloud vanishes as quickly as it appeared, taking the evil sorcerer with it. An oppressive silence fills the room. Exhausted, you slide down the wall. All that remains of Zargon is his crown and the royal sceptre...

300.text: You begin reading the tower guard's battered diary. It describes the siege from its first beginnings to its bitter end. The perceptive guard had noticed the disputes and power struggles between his master and Zargon long before King Richard could even imagine a coup. Yet even he could never have expected what was to come! Richard's ghost clearly wasn't exaggerating: while the king's body lay cold and twisted on the floor of Zargon's chamber, the sorcerer rounded up his former followers like cattle in the courtyard. There he offered them a choice: serve him, or follow their king into death. And there the diary ends... Cold anger cries out for revenge within you, mingled with desperate helplessness. You snap the little leather-bound book shut, unable to stare at that abrupt ending any longer. A thick grey cloud of dust rises from its yellowed pages. At that instant, lightning strikes the main tower outside, flooding the room with ghostly pale light for a fraction of a second and shaking the building to its foundations, as though a giant iron fist were trying to smash this nest of evil once and for all! It must have been much the same on the fateful night when the brave tower guard stood by his master for the very last time...

315.text: You stare up at the pale full moon as if in a trance, until a strange sound from the mountain to the north snaps you out of it. You've heard that sound before, in the overgrown graveyard of the ruined monastery. Only this time you aren't afraid. Quite the opposite: it feels strangely familiar, almost as though it were calling to you, drawing you in... Suddenly, a burning pain tears through your chest, as though some dark power were trying to possess you from within! Mad with pain, you reach to rip off your shirt - and freeze. Shaggy black hair covers your chest and arms. A few agonising seconds later, it covers your whole body! You try to scream, but the voice that comes out isn't yours. Instead of a human cry of pain, your throat gives forth a WOLF'S HOWL...! Frantically, you fight down the panic and try to think. Apparently, that wound the werewolf gave you during your midnight duel in the monastery graveyard wasn't quite as harmless as you'd naively assumed! You could kick yourself, but that won't help. Perhaps King Richard can find a cure once you escape this cursed castle. For now, you decide to put all thoughts of your hairy future on hold...

Or maybe Zargon is actually behind one of these pictures to amuse himself for a while before he finally sends you to your doom...?

364.text: You push the door handle down. A faint click sounds beneath your feet, and before you can jump back, a hidden trapdoor opens! At the last instant you catch the edge of the pit and try to haul yourself up. "I wish I hadn't skipped so many PE lessons!" you think desperately. Several exhausting attempts later, you realise you'll never get out without help. Looking down in panic, you see long iron spikes far below, crusted with dried blood. You open your mouth to shout, then realise that would only waste your breath. The only person who could hear you down here is Zargon, and you know exactly how much sympathy you'd get from him! Facing the hopelessness of your position, you say one last prayer and let go. A man has to know when it's time to leave... Unfortunately, the drop lasts longer than expected. Your head strikes the jagged rock walls again and again, yet you never quite lose consciousness. Then, suddenly, it's over. Impaled on the spikes, you let out a dying scream that shakes the castle, drowned out only by Zargon's mocking laughter...
